To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
14 kDA beta-galactose-binding lectin is a major protein that sugar-specifically binds endogenous glycoproteins of bovine grey matter.

the endogenous soluble glycoconjugates of the bovine brain grey mater, with molecular mass of 44, 60, and 123 kDa, can sugar-specifically interact with the 14 kDa lectin from the same tissue, and that this lectin is the only protein from the same source that can sugar-specifically bind to the above mentioned soluble glycoproteines.
the 14 kDa lectin from bovin brain grey matter is the only endogenous soluble protein that can sugar-specifically interact with N-linked glycoprotein receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of endogenous glycoproteins that interact with BBL.
the isolation and identification of endogenous soluble N-linked glycoprotein receptors from bovine brain.

the identification of endogenous glycoproteins that are able to sugar-specifically interact with BBL, and with the identification of a possible physiological function of this lectin in the nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BBL is the endogenous lectin of the brain, that is, it is the major protein that sugar-specifically binds endogenous soluble glycosylated proteins in the brain, and that it is not a contaminant of brain tissue.
14 kDA beta-galactose-binding lectin is an endogenous glycoproteins of bovine brain gray matter.

14 kD beta-galacto-side-binding lectin, which has been purified and characterized from bovine brain, is an ubiquitous glycoprotein that is present in the brain of different species and that it has a sugar-specific interaction with its endogenous glycoproteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 14 kDa lectin from bovin brain grey matter is a major protein that interacts with endogenous N-linked soluble glycoproteons in brain grey matter.
BBL is a soluble lectin of bovine brain that interacts with endogenous N-linked oligosaccharides of glycoproteins.
the 14 kDa BBL is a major endogenous glycoproteic ligand for the endogenous N-linked soluble glycoproteic receptors in bovine brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
14 kDA beta-galactose-binding lectin is a protein of the bovine brain grey mater that can interact sugar-specifically with endogenous soluble N-linked glycoprotein receptors.
14 kDA beta-galactose-binding lectin is a major protein in brain grey matter, which interacts sugar-specifically with endogenous glycoproteins.
BBL can be sugar-specifically recognized by endogenous N-linked oligosaccharide chains.
